channel.title: The Replicant Truth
channel.description: News and analysis from the world of physical artificial intelligence.

item.title: Why changing tools can help a robot handle different jobs
item.description: Imagine stirring a salad, turning food in a pan and cutting an ingredient. One tool would be awkward for all three jobs. Researchers designed a robot interface that changes ordinary tools without replacing the whole arm. The work appeared on October 29 and describes a laboratory system rather than a ready-made kitchen assistant.

item.title: How a four-legged robot learns to pull a wagon around obstacles
item.description: Pulling a suitcase around a corner can be harder than walking around the corner yourself. The wheels may catch an obstacle even when you pass safely. A four-legged robot pulling a wagon faces a similar problem. Researchers built a navigation system that considers the path of both the robot and its trailer.

item.title: How can we compare robots that demonstrate different tricks?
item.description: One robot moves blocks quickly while another carefully lifts a delicate object. Which is better? A single success number cannot answer that when the tasks and testing conditions differ. Researchers proposed a framework that asks readers to look more closely at what each experiment actually measured.

item.title: Why a soft robot gripper should tolerate small mistakes
item.description: When you pick up a cup, your fingers adjust a little to its shape. A robot benefits from similar flexibility, especially if its camera estimates the object's position imperfectly. Researchers proposed designing soft grippers for these small errors rather than assuming that every approach will be perfectly aligned.

item.title: A five-finger robot tries packing an online order
item.description: Packing an online order means choosing the correct products, placing them in a box and avoiding damage. At an event in Tokyo, a company demonstrated a robot with a five-finger hand doing similar work. The event took place on October 27 and 28, while the company reported it on October 30.

item.title: From isolated tricks to verifiable work
item.description: Research and demonstrations expand the range of robot actions, but the strength of the result depends on test conditions.

item.title: Why a talking robot can begin its reply sooner
item.description: Imagine a conversation where the other person stays silent for a long time before every answer. Even a good answer would feel awkward. On October 30, a Japanese company announced an update to a tabletop talking robot. It can now begin speaking the first part of a reply while the rest is still being prepared.

item.title: How five cameras can help a machine see its surroundings
item.description: Looking at an object with two eyes helps you judge distance. Two cameras can use a similar clue: their pictures differ slightly, and software can estimate how far away something is. On October 27, developers introduced a small board that connects up to five cameras. The cameras can be placed in different parts of a robot.

item.title: Why a talking robot can begin its reply sooner
item.description: Japan's Vstone announced an October 30 update allowing a tabletop robot to play the first parts of its spoken reply while later parts are still being prepared.
